datasets.name: Nexar Collision Prediction
datasets.annotations: Per-clip collision/near-miss label and event/alert times (paper arXiv:2503.03848)
datasets.clips: Train: 1,500 clips (about 750 positive collision/near-miss, 750 negative), about 40 s each; test: about 10 s clips cut 0.5/1.0/1.5 s before the event
datasets.clip_format: Real dashcam video, 1280x720 at 30 fps; metadata columns label, time_of_event, time_of_alert, light_conditions, weather, scene
datasets.access: Gated on Hugging Face: login, acceptance of the Nexar licence and sharing contact details. Acceptance must be done by the user

terms.statement: Free use with copyright notice retained; no sale, sublicensing or redistribution for profit without written consent from Nexar; attribution and citation required; no re-identification of people or vehicles, including by cross-referencing; no systems intended to cause harm or simulate unsafe driving; no termination clause

datasets.dashcam_relevance: Highest of the candidates: real forward dashcams, unedited
datasets.storage_estimate: About 31.4 GB total (dataset card). Sample of 16 x 40 s training clips at 720p: about 0.3-0.5 GB (expectation from typical bitrates; confirm by file listing)
datasets.notes: Positive labels mix collisions and near-misses in one class and give one event time, so they score collision timing only partially; approach and cut-in labels must be added by our own annotators. Licence does not explicitly address training a model shipped free of charge; ask Nexar in writing before any training use.

datasets.name: Detection of Traffic Anomaly (DoTA)
datasets.annotations: Per-clip JSON in dataset/DoTA_annotations.zip (10.4 MB, 4,677 files, checked 2026-10-17): video_name, channel, num_frames, ignore, ego_involve, night, anomaly_start/end (clip frames at 10 fps; end exclusive in 4,337 files, inclusive in 340), video_start/end, accident_id/accident_name (10 anomaly categories plus normal) and per-frame objects (obj_track_id, xyxy bbox, category, trunc). Objects occur only on anomaly frames: they are the anomaly participants, not every road user
datasets.clips: 4,677 clips (61 marked ignore), about 55 GB as frames (Google Drive split zips) or by YouTube URL list; no per-clip official download; 6 source videos removed from YouTube
datasets.clip_format: YouTube dashcam compilations, downloaded by URL list; annotations at 10 fps; 1280x720 typical
datasets.access: Google Drive archives or YouTube download script (requires YouTube cookies); no small official subset

terms.statement: Repository code MIT. No explicit dataset licence; authors state channel owners permitted sharing. Video rights remain with YouTube uploaders

datasets.dashcam_relevance: Medium: real dashcams but edited compilations with cuts and overlays
datasets.storage_estimate: Not published; estimate tens of GB for all videos (hypothesis)
datasets.notes: Blocked: video rights belong to YouTube uploaders; author statement of channel permission is not a licence to us; downloading via YouTube scripts conflicts with YouTube terms. Annotation metadata imported by evaluation/importers/dota.py as source labels only: categories are anomaly types, not our event types, and participants cannot score detection.

datasets.name: Car Crash Dataset (CCD)
datasets.annotations: Accident start frame, ego-involved flag, day/night, weather, object boxes
datasets.clips: 1,500 accident clips plus 3,000 normal clips (normal clips from BDD100K)
datasets.clip_format: 50 frames at 10 fps (5 s); YouTube sources for accidents

terms.statement: Repository MIT; dataset terms unstated; underlying YouTube and BDD100K footage carries its own terms

datasets.dashcam_relevance: Low-medium: 5 s at 10 fps is far from 30 fps continuous footage; no context before the event
datasets.notes: Useful for condition breakdowns (day/night, weather). The 10 fps rate limits timing-error and jerk measurements.

datasets.name: Dashcam Accident Dataset (DAD)
datasets.annotations: Accident clip label with accident in the last frames; object tracks for some objects
datasets.clips: about 1,750 clips of 100 frames (620 positive) per the original paper; to verify
datasets.clip_format: YouTube dashcam footage from Taiwan, 20 fps, 1280x720 per paper; to verify
datasets.notes: Lowest priority; overlaps with CCD and DoTA.

datasets.name: BDD100K
datasets.annotations: Frame-level boxes, drivable area, lanes, weather/time-of-day/scene tags; no incident labels
datasets.clip_format: Real phone dashcam video, 720p at 30 fps
datasets.access: Registration at bdd-data.berkeley.edu (unreachable from this machine on 2026-10-16)

terms.statement: Data and labels: UC Regents grant use, copy, modify and distribute for educational, research and not-for-profit purposes; commercial use only for BDD and BAIR Commons members and affiliates, otherwise by licence from UC Berkeley OTL. Code: BSD-3-Clause

datasets.dashcam_relevance: High for normal driving and condition variety (night, rain, curves)
datasets.storage_estimate: Full video set about 1.8 TB (published figure, secondary); a 50-clip sample is about 1-2 GB (hypothesis)
datasets.notes: Blocked for a commercially compatible product unless UC Berkeley OTL grants a licence or Spectra qualifies as not-for-profit (legal question).

datasets.name: Own and consented user footage

terms.statement: Written consent per contributor, including bystander privacy terms

datasets.notes: Only realistic source of labelled approach and cut-in events in normal, unedited footage.

datasets.name: Wikimedia Commons, Category:Dashcam videos
datasets.clip_format: WebM, mostly 1280x720 or 1920x1080, 7 s to 5 min

terms.statement: Per-file licence. Incident clips mostly {{PD-CCTV}} (public-domain claim that automatic camera footage lacks human authorship; re-uploads from Douyin and Reddit). Normal-driving clips own work under CC BY-SA 4.0 / CC BY 4.0 / CC BY 3.0

datasets.dashcam_relevance: High: real dashcams, short clips; some re-encoded, cropped or watermarked
datasets.notes: PD-CCTV rests on a jurisdiction-dependent no-human-authorship theory and the provenance chain (Douyin/Reddit uploader) is unverified; low risk for internal evaluation without redistribution, owner decision required. CC BY/BY-SA require attribution if redistributed. Contains identifiable people and plates: keep local, no re-identification.

datasets.name: comma2k19
datasets.annotations: No event labels; CAN speed, steering, radar, IMU, GNSS and poses in the full chunks
datasets.clips: 2,019 one-minute segments, 33 h, California highway commute
datasets.access: Public Hugging Face (not gated); full data as about 10 GB zip chunks; one standalone 37.5 MB segment under compression_challenge/
datasets.dashcam_relevance: Medium-high: real forward camera, mostly one highway route
datasets.storage_estimate: One segment 37.5 MB; a full chunk about 10 GB
datasets.notes: Only permissively licensed real driving source found. CAN radar lead distance in full chunks could support weak approach labels later (would need a 10 GB chunk approval).

datasets.name: PREVENTION (UAH)
datasets.annotations: Per drive (processed_data.zip, members stored uncompressed; readable by HTTP range): detection_camera1/lane_changes.txt (id_l id_d type f0 fe ff blk), logs/log_camera1.txt (cloud frame t0 t1, t0 in microseconds), detections_tracked.txt (authors' detector), lanes.txt, labels.txt and trajectories.txt (empty on RECORD4/DRIVE3). Released types: 3 left 381, 4 right 468, 5 hazardous 2, 6 pedestrian 1; no cut-in (1) or cut-out (2) labels. Surrounding vehicles only
event_coverage: lane_change of surrounding vehicles (target lane not stated)
datasets.clips: 5 records, 11 drives of 7-52 min (about 6 h); front and rear cameras, LiDAR, radar
datasets.clip_format: Front camera mp4 per drive (192.8 MB to 1.44 GB); camera log gives 10.7-11.7 fps
datasets.access: Direct download, no account. RECORD4/DRIVE3 (smallest, 18 lane changes): video_camera1.mp4 192,798,168 B; processed_data.zip 365,621,255 B, of which lane_changes.txt 882 B, log_camera1.txt 227,280 B, detections_tracked.txt 24,866,683 B, lanes.txt 952,626 B (Content-Length and zip directory, 2026-10-17)
datasets.dashcam_relevance: Medium: one calibrated research vehicle on Spanish highways; real lane changes of surrounding traffic
datasets.storage_estimate: 193 MB for the RECORD4/DRIVE3 front video; about 25 MB more for its tracked detections
datasets.notes: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: private, non-commercial evaluation; labels and clips stay in evaluation/restricted/ and are not redistributed with the MIT code. Owner decision on evaluation_use pending. RECORD4/DRIVE1 and DRIVE2 camera logs have missed-carry timestamp defects. id_l/id_d meaning unconfirmed.
